blocks.text: Constitutional AI is an alignment approach that replaces much of the direct human labeling used in RLHF, covered in an earlier topic, with a written set of principles, a constitution, that the model itself uses to critique and revise its own responses.

This topic covers how a constitution guides model behavior, the two training phases constitutional AI typically uses, and how it compares to the more human-feedback-heavy alignment methods covered earlier in this module.
1. Reducing Reliance on Direct Human Labels

blocks.alt: Human label heavy RLHF is compared against constitution guided training

blocks.text: RLHF, covered in an earlier topic, depends heavily on human labelers judging individual model outputs, constitutional AI instead encodes the judging criteria directly into a written document, then has the model apply that document to itself, reducing how much per-example human labeling the process needs.
2. What a Constitution Actually Is

blocks.alt: Written principles together form a constitution

blocks.text: A constitution, in this context, is a set of written principles, statements like preferring responses that are honest, avoiding harmful content, respecting user autonomy, that the model is trained to consult when evaluating its own outputs, rather than relying purely on implicit patterns learned from labeled examples.

blocks.text: 3. Self-Critique and Revision

blocks.alt: A model draft response goes through self critique against the constitution, producing a revised response

blocks.text: In the first phase, the model generates an initial response, then critiques that same response against the constitution principles, then produces a revised response that better satisfies those principles, all without a human labeler intervening at any step.
This critique-then-revise loop can run for multiple rounds, each pass typically producing a response that adheres more closely to the stated principles than the one before it.
4. The Two Training Phases

blocks.alt: A supervised phase of critique and revise is followed by an RL phase using AI feedback

blocks.text: Constitutional AI typically runs in two phases, a supervised phase where the model is fine-tuned directly on its own critiqued and revised responses, followed by a reinforcement learning phase, often called RLAIF, where AI-generated preference judgments, rather than human ones, drive a process structurally similar to RLHF reward modeling and PPO, both covered in earlier topics.
5. The Model as Both Generator and Judge

blocks.alt: The model acts as generator and also as judge, evaluating its own generated output

blocks.text: A distinctive feature of constitutional AI is that the same underlying model, or a closely related one, plays both roles, generating candidate responses and also judging which candidates better satisfy the constitution, a self-referential setup that would not make sense in RLHF, where a separate human judgment step is what grounds the reward model.

blocks.title: AI judging AI is the core structural shift
blocks.content: This self-judging setup is what allows constitutional AI to scale alignment feedback without a proportional increase in human labeling effort, though it depends heavily on the underlying model being capable enough to judge constitution adherence reliably.

blocks.text: 6. Constitutional AI vs RLHF

blocks.alt: Constitutional AI uses AI generated feedback while RLHF uses human generated feedback

blocks.text: The central comparison to RLHF, covered in an earlier topic, is where the feedback signal originates, RLHF grounds its reward model in direct human judgments of response quality, constitutional AI grounds its feedback in a written constitution applied by the model itself, trading some of RLHF human grounding for significantly reduced labeling cost.

blocks.text: 7. Designing Good Principles

blocks.alt: A vague or conflicting principle leads to inconsistent behavior while a clear principle leads to consistent behavior

blocks.text: The quality of a constitution matters directly, vague or mutually conflicting principles produce inconsistent self-critique, since the model has no clear way to resolve ambiguity, while clear, well scoped principles tend to produce more consistent and predictable revision behavior.
Writing an effective constitution is itself a nontrivial design task, closer to careful specification writing than to typical dataset curation covered elsewhere in this course.
8. When Constitutional AI Is a Good Fit

Constitutional AI tends to fit teams that need to scale alignment training without a proportional increase in human labeling budget, or that want alignment behavior grounded in an explicit, inspectable set of principles rather than an implicit pattern learned purely from labeled examples.
9. Practical Limitations

Because the judging model and the generating model are closely related, constitutional AI can propagate the underlying model existing blind spots or biases into its own self-critique, a limitation that direct human feedback in RLHF does not share in the same way, since human judgment provides an outside perspective the model itself lacks.
Worked Example

A team building a customer facing assistant writes a short constitution with principles favoring honesty, politeness, and avoiding overconfident claims. The model generates an initial response to a tricky support question, critiques it against those principles, catches an overconfident claim, and produces a revised response that flags uncertainty appropriately.

This critique-revise data is then used for a supervised fine-tuning pass, followed by an RLAIF phase where the model own preference judgments, again based on the constitution, drive further training, all without a human labeler reviewing each individual example.
Common Mistakes

items: Writing constitution principles that are vague enough to produce inconsistent self-critique
Assuming constitutional AI eliminates the need for any human oversight, when principle design itself still requires careful human judgment
Ignoring that a model self-critique inherits the same blind spots as its own generation, since no outside perspective is involved
Treating constitutional AI and RLHF as mutually exclusive rather than as approaches that can be combined in a single alignment pipeline

blocks.text: Practice

Draft three constitution style principles for a chatbot in a domain you are familiar with, then write one example response and manually critique it against your own principles, noting how specific or vague your principles turned out to be in practice.
Key Takeaway

Constitutional AI replaces much of RLHF direct human labeling with a written set of principles the model applies to critique and revise its own outputs, trading some human grounding for significantly reduced labeling cost, with the quality of the constitution itself becoming the main lever for how consistent and reliable the resulting alignment behavior is.
